result.title: E5 (KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1): own-event spike-breadth regime as a pre-registered partition of the frozen long detectors (F1_ARA, G2_RET30) under their recorded plan, in IDX, US and crypto
result.angle: REGIME / CROSS-MARKET: one regime variable fixed by convention before any number (cross-sectional frequency of the detector's own event, smoothed 20 sessions, versus its trailing 120-session median), applied as a label to the existing frozen signals with the plan unchanged; discovery gate requires the regime effect to hold WITHIN each discovery year (so that "regime" is not a renamed calendar-year effect); one validation run per cell on 2023; Bonferroni over 3 markets x 2 tests; cross-market lead-lag (US breadth -> crypto next UTC day / -> IDX next session) declared as a follow-on that needs a harness field and is NOT part of this test.
result.thesis: Every long run of the frozen detectors loses in aggregate, but the sign of the post-flag drift has moved with the market state: on IDX the E3 reference plan was +1.28% vs +0.26% matched in 2021 and -1.56% vs +0.03% in 2022 (research/E3/discovery/reference_summary.json); on crypto every one of 144 short plans was negative in 2021 and 143/144 positive in 2022 (E4 v1), and the BTC-bear short was admissible on discovery; E4 v2 then failed on 2023 because its regime was scarce there. Hypothesis: the drift after a flag is continuation when the market is in a speculative-participation state and reversal when it is not, and the cheapest decision-time measure of that state is the detector's own cross-sectional firing rate (ARA-lock count/tradeable names on IDX; +30%-day count/tradeable names on US and crypto), smoothed over the harness's standard 20 sessions and compared with its own trailing 120-session median (HOT if above, strict; COLD otherwise). Mechanism: when many names are locking limit-up or printing +30% days at once, attention and retail flow are broad, a flagged name is one of a cohort and the next sessions see follow-through; when spikes are isolated, the flagged name is an idiosyncratic pump or news print and the fade dominates (the mechanism E2/E4 measured: median 5-session move -10% vs 0% matched). The test is the interaction I = (rule - matched)_HOT - (rule - matched)_COLD under the plan already recorded for each detector, so the question is whether the flag's EXCESS drift over matched names depends on the state, not whether HOT markets go up. Design-time check of the regressor only (no returns computed; parameters fixed before the check; script in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-KOD-Machine/74d3ac27-b8ad-5917-a6c3-ea51c410b250/scratchpad/breadth_feasibility.py): crypto discovery 1,495 flags = E4's count exactly, HOT 1,052 / COLD 443 (2020 106/35, 2021 645/254, 2022 301/154); IDX discovery 1,919 flags = E3's count exactly, HOT 929 / COLD 990 (2021 728/612, 2022 201/378); US discovery (repair panel) 3,343 flags, HOT 1,947 / COLD 1,396 (2020 313/488 + 117 unlabelled in the 14 sessions before the trailing window is warm, 2021 758/567, 2022 876/341). Breadth is NOT the year dummy: only 54% of IDX 2021 flags are HOT and 72% of US 2022 flags are HOT, so the within-year interaction gate is a real test, not a replay of E3/E4's year splits.
result.why_not_already_falsified: (1) Signal family unchanged but information source new: no experiment has ever conditioned a LONG run of F1_ARA or G2_RET30 on any market-state variable; E1/E2/E3 trading results and the nine US repair reruns are aggregates over all sessions. (2) E4 v2's regime was a different variable (BTC close vs its 50-session mean, an index-trend proxy), a different side (short), a different plan family (pullback3/first_up/h2 under liquidation) and one market (crypto); its validation failure was a scarcity failure (34 scored). Breadth is own-event cross-sectional frequency, computed inside every market from its own panel (no BTC row needed, no index/ETF needed: ETFs are dropped from the US universe by idxsig/sources/us_universe.py line 42, so an index-trend regime on US is not even available), and its trailing-median construction gives roughly half the sessions in each cell (HOT session share 0.50 crypto, 0.37 IDX, 0.44 US on discovery) instead of a regime that mostly waits. (3) The E3 REPORT (research/E3/REPORT.md lines 63-67) names exactly this condition for IDX ("trade only when the market-wide ARA count is above its trailing median ... designed without looking at 2023 and tested once on it") and the project map lists it as never run; E5 is that proposal generalised to the three markets with the admission and testing rules written down. (4) The per-year numbers that motivated the hypothesis are NOT what the test measures: the discovery gate requires the interaction inside each calendar year, and the feasibility counts show breadth splits each year roughly 55/45 to 70/30, so a pass cannot be produced by the 2021-vs-2022 difference alone. (5) The crypto long on 2023 (E2: -1.90% vs +1.42% matched) was mostly a BTC-bull year, which approximately falsifies "index bull -> long" there; it says nothing about own-event breadth, which varies inside 2023 by construction.

protocol.family: KOD-GLOBAL-E5-v1: regime partition, not a plan search. Rule module idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py copies the detector code verbatim (moonshot_e1 features/flags for IDX, moonshot_g for US/CRYPTO, as moonshot_e3/e4 do; tests check flags identical to the originals) and exposes, per market base detector X, three rules: E5_X_ALL (= X; reproduces the pinned run), E5_X_HOT (= X & HOT_d), E5_X_COLD (= X & regime evaluable & ~HOT_d). Regime definition frozen in research/E5/protocol.json before any statistic: B_d = (# tradeable names with the base event at d) / (# tradeable names at d), with event = lock_up & tradeable on IDX and ret1 >= 0.30 & tradeable on US/CRYPTO (the frozen flag itself, no new threshold); S_d = mean(B_{d-19..d}) (20 = controls.LOOKBACK, the harness convention); M_d = median(S_{d-120..d-1}) with all 120 values required (120 chosen because it is the longest window warm by the US discovery start; 250 was considered and is declared NOT run); HOT_d = S_d > M_d (strict; ties COLD); sessions where M_d is undefined are unlabelled and their flags belong to neither cell (expected: US 2020-07-01..2020-07-21 only). The regime is session-level, uses sessions <= d only (prefix-first causal check applies), returns NaN where not tradeable so controls draw from every tradeable name on the same session exactly as for the base rule. Stages (idxsig/e5.py cloned from e3.py/e4.py, each stage a new exist_ok=False directory under research/E5/<market>/): e5-reproduce (precondition: re-run the three pinned runs on the current panels; REPRODUCED/DEVIATES recorded; --accept-deviation allowed only for the known 4th-decimal matched-baseline deviation from controls.py bcb89f0, as E3 did), e5-regime (writes research/E5/regime/<market>/calendar_discovery.csv: date, B, S, M, HOT, flags_count; sha256 stamped into every later output; committed before discovery; no return in the file), e5-discovery (3 rules x 1 plan per market = 9 harness runs; plans.csv; partition_check.json; gate), e5-validation (the same 3 rules per market on 2023 as recorded write_run runs, 9 runs, one pass; validation calendar computed at this stage only). Partition check (abort on failure): every attempted trade of the ALL run appears in exactly one of HOT/COLD with identical ticker, signal_date, status, entry/exit and net_return; trades present in HOT u COLD but not in ALL must be exactly the ALL run's SKIP_OVERLAP signals (overlap='skip' is per name, so a COLD hold cannot block a HOT signal in the HOT-only run); counts reported.
detectors: F1_ARA (IDX; MOONSHOT_E1_D1 v1.1 code verbatim) -> E5_F1_ARA_ALL / _HOT / _COLD
G2_RET30 (US; MOONSHOT_E2_US_D1 v1 code verbatim) -> E5_G2_RET30_ALL / _HOT / _COLD
G2_RET30 (CRYPTO; MOONSHOT_E2_CRYPTO_D1 v1 code verbatim) -> E5_G2_RET30_ALL / _HOT / _COLD
protocol.plans: The plan already recorded for each detector, unchanged, one per market, no grid: IDX entry at the next close (entry_lag 1), exit at the 5th close, fill model A, ca_mode registry, Rp10,000,000, 10% participation, config pinned to results/runs/20261008T000401Z_MOONSHOT_E1_D1_v1.1 (config sha 34a0d8d7...); CRYPTO entry at the next UTC-day open, exit at the 5th close, fill A, ca_mode adjusted, $5,000, pinned to 20261008T005732Z_MOONSHOT_E2_CRYPTO_D1_v1 (86bd8d48...); US entry at the next open, exit at the 5th close, fill B, units as_traded, quarantine unit_schedule, repair panel panel_us_repair-20261008T114805Z (sha 8d3b7ce4...), pinned to 20261008T115656Z_MOONSHOT_E2_US_D1_v1 (the run the live paper decisions cite). Discovery uses the identical config on the discovery window. No entry/exit rule, window, hold, fill model, notional or cost may differ between ALL/HOT/COLD or between stages. 200 matched draws, seed 20261007, controls v2, overlap skip, data_end_exit last_close (as every pinned run).
protocol.discovery_period: IDX 2021-01-22..2022-12-30 (TIER_1); US and CRYPTO 2020-07-01..2022-12-31 (E2 periods); regime warm-up read from the panel start (IDX 2019-07-29, US 2020-01-02, CRYPTO 2020-01-01) for B/S/M only. Discovery is in-sample for the base detectors (E2/E3 addenda) and is used here as a GATE, not for selection: there is nothing to select.
protocol.validation_period: IDX 2023-01-02..2023-12-29; US and CRYPTO 2023-01-01..2023-12-31 (E2/E3 validation windows, VALIDATION_WINDOWS in paper.py). Explicitly declared: the 2023 AGGREGATE outcomes of all three base runs are already recorded (IDX -4.06% vs -0.53%; CRYPTO -1.90% vs +1.42%; US -0.97% vs -0.75%), no regime-split statistic of any of them exists anywhere in the repo, and crypto 2023 has already carried one regime-conditioned test (E4 v2, short, BTC regime). Prior regime looks per validation set: IDX 0, US 0, CRYPTO 1. Holdout (IDX 2024-01-02..2025-02-21; US/CRYPTO 2024-01-01 on) never loaded: e5.py asserts end <= the validation end for every market before building a RunConfig (HEAD has no GLOBAL_HOLDOUT code guard for US/CRYPTO; merging PR #7 first adds it).
protocol.admissibility: Tests per market, all one-sided, family-wise alpha 0.05 Bonferroni over 3 markets x 2 tests = 6 -> alpha_adj = 0.00833 (above the 200-draw floor 0.004975, so attainable). T1 (information): I = (avg_net_HOT - matched_mean_HOT) - (avg_net_COLD - matched_mean_COLD) > 0, p < alpha_adj from a pre-registered calendar-week block bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 20261015) over per-trade excess returns (net_return - per-trade matched mean over the 200 draws, the new trades column), one-sided p = share of resamples with I* <= 0. T2 (tradability of the HOT cell, E3/E4 rules unchanged): scored_HOT >= 200 on discovery / >= 100 on validation, avg_net_HOT > 0, avg_net_HOT > matched_mean_HOT, harness p_one_sided_vs_matched < alpha_adj, and on discovery avg_net_HOT > 0 in every discovery year with >= 50 scored. DISCOVERY GATE (validation is run in a market only if it passes): T1 on the pooled discovery window AND I_y > 0 (point estimate, from by_year rule and random_matched means) in every discovery calendar year with >= 50 scored in both HOT and COLD (expected from the feasibility counts: 2021 and 2022 in all markets; 2020 in crypto COLD ~35 flags may fall below 50 and is then not required). If the gate fails, the market's validation is NOT run and 2023 is not touched for it. VALIDATION PASS: T1 at alpha_adj. T2 is reported in every market but may be CLAIMED only where its discovery version also passed. CLAIM LEVELS declared in advance: IDX and US (first regime look on their 2023) = validation-grade; CRYPTO (second regime look on its 2023) = 'informative, needs prospective confirmation' whatever the p. CONSEQUENCES: pass -> no paper BUY and no policy change from this result alone; it licenses (a) a new PAPER-POLICY version that records the HOT/COLD label on every DECISION (computed from the scan's own 200-day bar pull with the identical 20/120 rule; label only, decisions unchanged) and pre-registers the prospective test (E30 rate and r5 of HOT vs COLD decisions, >= 100 scored HOT decisions before any reading), (b) a holdout-final test only after that prospective evidence, per E4 v2's own closing statement. Fail -> own-event breadth carries no decision-time information about the flag's excess drift for that detector; this protocol states that NO other regime variable may be tested on that market's 2023 for these detectors (the regime look is spent) and any further regime idea is prospective-only. Regime-variable budget declared: candidates considered at design time were (i) own-event breadth [tested], (ii) index trend (BTC 50d / equal-weight panel index) [not tested; E4 v2 tested the short side of it on crypto], (iii) cross-sectional volatility (VIX proxy) [not tested], (iv) cross-market US breadth [not tested; needs a harness field]; only (i) is run and (ii)-(iv) are barred from 2023 by this protocol.
protocol.matched_controls: The harness's own matched random baseline unchanged: for each attempted signal, 200 draws on the SAME session from tradeable names in the same price_band / liquidity / market_cap (IDX) / volatility / momentum / drawdown / listing_age buckets (controls v2, relaxed to >= 5 names), executed under the identical plan. Because the regime is a session-level variable and controls are drawn on the signal's session, every control shares the signal's regime by construction, so (rule - matched) inside a cell is the flag's excess drift given the state, and I is the regime x flag interaction net of the state's effect on all comparable names. Same-session uniform baseline reported as secondary. Known non-match: sector (not point-in-time); HOT episodes can be sector frenzies, which the controls do not hold fixed (declared limitation).
protocol.costs_model: Exactly the pinned runs' profiles (idxsig/profiles.py): IDX fees 0.15% buy / 0.25% sell, lot 100, ARA lock refuses entry; US price-tier cost per side (1.5% <$1, 0.5% $1-5, 0.15% $5-20, 0.05% above) plus SEC fee on sales, no borrow (long only); CRYPTO 0.1% fee + 0.1% slippage per side. No price impact, no dividends. Long only (the short side is declared exhausted on crypto by E4 v2 and not realistically borrowable for US microcaps).

Optional, after validation: paper.py new POLICY_ID (v5) recording the breadth label on DECISION records from the scan's own bar pull; not part of this experiment and a separate owner decision. Declared follow-on E5b (not run): cross-market lead-lag (US breadth at the US close -> crypto next UTC day; crypto UTC-day breadth -> IDX same-day session) requires a session-level exogenous field added to Market/RULE_FIELDS/CausalSource with its own prefix-first check (~6-8 h) and would be a NEW protocol with its own alpha accounting.
result.falsifier: Discovery kill (no 2023 touched): in a market, I <= 0 on the pooled discovery window, or I_y <= 0 in any discovery calendar year with >= 50 scored trades in both HOT and COLD cells -- i.e. the flag's excess drift over matched names is not larger in HOT than in COLD inside the year, so "regime" was only the calendar year. Validation kill (the exact result that ends the regime idea for these detectors): on 2023 in IDX and in US (the first-look markets), I <= 0 or the calendar-week block-bootstrap one-sided p >= 0.00833; equivalently, the HOT-cell rule-minus-matched is not better than the COLD-cell rule-minus-matched by more than block-resampling noise. A HOT cell with fewer than 100 scored trades fails T2 for the right reason and is recorded as such (not retried with another window). Any of these outcomes closes own-event breadth as a decision-time switch for F1_ARA/G2_RET30, bars every other regime variable from these validation sets, and leaves only prospective evidence for any regime claim.
risks: Consumed validation year: the 2023 aggregates of the three base runs are known to everyone on the project; the regime split is new but it is a conditional analysis on seen data. Mitigations are structural (parameter-free-by-convention regime, calendar committed before any outcome, partition of already-recorded trades, discovery gate that can kill before 2023) and the claim levels are downgraded accordingly (crypto explicitly a second look). A sceptic may still weigh IDX/US passes below a fresh-year pass; the protocol says so and routes any pass to prospective confirmation before the holdout.

Cell size in 2023 is unknown by design (not computed here); if a market's HOT cell has < 100 scored trades the tradability test fails for the right reason (E4 v2 precedent) while T1 can still be read.

US leg inherits E2's repair limitations: pre-2023 unit factors are provider records not SEC-corroborated (discovery gate on unverified units, declared); the 669-name quarantine is outcome-correlated (repair_v3 SELECTION_NOTE) and is the same filter in both cells but not guaranteed regime-neutral; survivor-only universe flatters longs in both cells.

Matched controls do not hold sector fixed; HOT episodes may be sector frenzies (e.g. microcap AI in 2023) whose cohort momentum the controls partly miss, which could bias I upward; the same-session baseline and a declared post-hoc descriptive (no claim) by price band are the only checks.

Overlap='skip' makes HOT u COLD a superset of the ALL run's attempted trades by exactly the ALL run's SKIP_OVERLAP signals (IDX 67, US 82, CRYPTO ~6 on 2023); the partition check reports them and they are kept in the cells (declared), so cell sums do not reproduce the ALL average to the last trade.

Mechanical bias: the signal's own flag enters B_d on one of the 20 smoothing sessions (1/4,300 US, 1/690 IDX, 1/250 crypto per flag); negligible but declared; the alternative (exclude the own name) would make the regime name-specific and break the shared-session control property.
IDX precondition will DEVIATE in the 4th decimal of the matched baseline (controls.py bcb89f0, as E3 found); accepted only for that known cause; any deviation on the rule side aborts.

Harness change (two new trades.csv columns) touches backtest.run; must be committed and tested before any E5 run because write_run refuses a dirty tree and the rule hash/verify-runs must stay valid; old runs unaffected.
Compute: 21 harness runs (3 reproduce + 18), the six US runs on the 4.4M-row repair panel with 200 draws are the slow ones; IDX panel must be rebuilt first (build-panel refuses if raw hashes differ).

Interpretation risk: a positive I with negative avg_net_HOT means the regime is informative but not tradeable under this plan; the protocol separates the two claims so neither can be dressed as the other, and no plan search is allowed afterwards on these windows.
result.directive_compliance: Holdout: never loaded; every RunConfig end is asserted <= 2023-12-29 (IDX) / 2023-12-31 (US, CRYPTO) inside e5.py, the IDX HOLDOUT guard in backtest.py applies, and merging PR #7 first adds the GLOBAL_HOLDOUT code guard for US/CRYPTO; nothing in this proposal reads, summarises or computes on 2024+. No retune: detector code copied verbatim (E3/E4 pattern, test-checked), no threshold searched (the regime event IS the frozen flag), regime parameters fixed by convention and justified before any statistic (20 = harness LOOKBACK, 120 = longest window warm at the US discovery start, strict > median), the discovery-window regime calendar is committed before discovery, the plan is the recorded one, and HOT/COLD are a partition of trades the harness already recorded. No manufactured results: this proposal contains no return, hit rate or p from any window; the only numbers computed were flag and session counts by regime on discovery windows (regressor distribution, no outcomes), reported as such with the script path. Pre-registration: research/E5/protocol.json with sha stamped in every stage output, stages created exist_ok=False under the append-only research/ guard, dirty-tree refusal, the six tests and alpha_adj = 0.00833 fixed in advance, claim levels and the regime-variable budget declared, consequences on pass (label-only policy version + prospective test, then holdout-final) and on fail (regime family closed for these detectors on these windows) written before the first run. Read-only session: nothing in /home/user/KOD-Machine was modified; the feasibility script lives in the scratchpad.
result.expected_information_value: Either way the project learns whether the time variation that every long and short run has shown (hot 2021 vs cold 2022; E4's bear-only admissibility) is a market state knowable at the decision from the panel itself. Pass (I > 0 at alpha_adj in IDX/US): the paper ledger gains a legitimate, pre-registered on/off label for the three live scans and a concrete prospective test (HOT vs COLD E30 rate and r5 over the next ~6 months at the observed ~95 IDX / ~200 US / ~65 crypto decisions per month), which is the first path to a paper BUY that does not require a new detector family; it also tells E3-style plan work where to look (HOT cell only) if ever reopened on new data. Fail: the last cheap regime idea for the frozen detectors is closed with a documented look, the year effects are shown not to be forecastable from own-event breadth, and the regime-variable budget statement stops the drift toward a second and third regime variable on the same 2023 data; effort then goes to prospective evidence or genuinely new signal families (prior-volatility early detection, catalyst feeds). The within-year gate adds a third outcome: breadth tracks the year but not the within-year variation, which would say the regime is slow (yearly) and not actionable at 20-session resolution. The experiment costs about three working days and no new data, and it leaves the holdout and the prospective ledger untouched.
